additional_info.subject: ID0480099-DC/Si-D/AT-[Multi] Cooling issue CRM:02889001160
additional_info.body:
Dear Johannes,
Thank you for contacting our eMobility Support, I hope this email finds you well.
Following your request we could check the charge sessions and regarding this "maximum current of charging cable is limited by under temperature" we could find more information.
It is expected to have the charging current is limited to 250A in case temperature of coolant feed or coolant return is below 0°C.
The pump has temperature sensors, which needs to be read out by the EVSE to determine the present maximum current, which the EV is allowed to consume. This is especially important for low temperatures, when the coolant has high viscosity. At temperatures below -8°C the pump automatically turns on a heater inside the tank. It remains on until the temperature increased to >=+2°C.
Due to the current ambient temperatures at the chargers' location, once the chargers' temperature dropped below 0°C the maximum current was limited as expected - once the fans were shutdown the temperature increased back to normal operating levels, without the need to turn on the heater. In situations where the temperature does not increase as expected after fan shutdown, the heater is engaged to bring it back up.
With best regards,
eMobility Technical
Support Team – Felipe Moraes
Please do not change the subject line when replying to this email.

additional_info.subject: ID0480099-DC/Si-D/AT-[Multi] Cooling issue CRM:02889001160
additional_info.body:
Dear Johannes,
I hope this email finds you well.
Complementing the last email
Why are so many chargers affected?
The cable should heat itself while being used, but since it is cold, the PLC send the informative that it is limit by 100A or 250A because of the temperature and since the other chargers are in the same weather it can also affect then.
Can we check whether the heater of the cooling unit is functioning properly?
The cooling doesn't have a heater as its purpose to cool down the charging cables - as for heating the charging cables this should occur normally during the charging process.
We should ensure that the heater is activated in time, even at temperatures of 0 or −5 °C, to avoid any loss of power
The cable should heat it self while charging because the "heater" is related with the charger, and the cable only has a colling system that doesn't heats.
So where exactly does the problem lie?
In resume. in the charger we don't have problems, the charger has a heater in case the temperature is below 0 ºC, the cable doesn't have a heater because it heats after start to be used.
With best regards,
eMobility Technical Support Team – Felipe Moraes
Please do not change the subject line when replying to this email.

additional_info.body:
HI Johannes,
I hope this email finds you well.
Thank you for your patience, I could check the screenshots you shared and needed to confirm with Francisco.
Apologies from the information I have shared before.
The heather in the cooling system turns on when the cable temperature is -8 or below or if the car requests 100A or more.
On these situation we see on the logs that we have a limit on the power delivery, and 2 minutes later as we could see on the logs, the limit is removed and the car charges as normal.
I asked a screenshot to explain better how it works
On this screenshot we can see that is needed determine the maximum current from the EV, apart from this if the temperature is below -8ºC the pump automatically turns on the heater inside the tank.
With be
st regards,
